title: Non-Asymptotic Confidence Intervals for Neural Network Predictions via Sequential Parameter Estimation and Conformal Prediction
content: Reliable uncertainty quantification for neural network predictions remains an open challenge, especially when data are scarce and the noise distribution is unknown. Existing methods either rely on asymptotic approximations, require extensive retraining, or lack formal finite‑sample guarantees. We propose a hybrid approach that bridges non‑asymptotic sequential parameter estimation with distribution‑free conformal prediction. The key innovation is a data‑driven stopping rule: we monitor the average width of predictions obtained from models whose validation loss falls within a theoretically derived confidence region. The required constants—the Lipschitz constant, the strong convexity parameter, the noise variance, and the parameter‑space diameter—are estimated on‑the‑fly from the stochastic gradient descent trajectory, avoiding any prior knowledge of the model. When the average prediction width drops below a user‑specified threshold, training stops, and the final model is used for split conformal calibration on the validation set. Experiments on a synthetic sinusoidal regression and the Boston Housing dataset show that the method achieves coverage of at least 95% in all scenarios. In the synthetic case with an attainable accuracy, training stops early (at epoch 54), while for a stringent tolerance it continues to the end, demonstrating that the rule adapts to the problem without false alarms. The approach is computationally efficient, requires only a single training run, and offers rigorous finite‑sample coverage guarantees without distributional assumptions.
